failures.criterion: A1 and the change's own goal: Go reads such a document as the engine does, or refuses it by name; a document and a comment holding the same markdown read alike. An image whose label holds an inline HTML declaration loses the declaration's characters: `![p <!a> q](i.png)` is stored as `![p  q](i.png)`.
failures.evidence:
Regression against main, found by the branch's own differential over a 452-document corpus of my own ($TMPDIR/tester752/adversarial-corpus.ts, the shapes gen/leaf-marks-corpus.ts does not write): `bash differential.sh --base 2b427f930eace9e2007ab970e0b79013637deee7 --corpus $TMPDIR/tester752/corpus --out $TMPDIR/tester752/out` -> FAIL, `GATE regressions 9`, `GATE churn 9`, `GATE engine-tree churn 9`, `GATE lost fixed points 9`, every one `![p <!a> q](i.png)` in one of the nine containers (report.jsonl ids adv:adv-392..400). The dumps of the two revisions for `![p <!a> q](i.png)`: base tree `{"type":"image","attrs":{"alt":"p <!a> q","src":"i.png"}}` rendering `![p <!a> q](i.png)`, head tree alt `p  q` rendering `![p  q](i.png)`, `base_reads_as_engine true`, `head_reads_as_engine false`. The engine of this head reads the alt `p <!a> q` (gen/differential.ts). On the real surface, with the Dispatch e2e harness (real Go server, production SPA bundle, real Postgres), a spec and a comment both holding `![p <!a> q](i.png)` and `![r <b> s](i.png)`: the stored spec came back `# Alt

![p  q](i.png)

![r  s](i.png)
`, the comment drew alt `["p <!a> q","r <b> s"]` and the spec editor `["p  q","r  s"]` - the document and the comment now read differently, which is the defect this issue was filed for. Cause: `parseImage` (packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/pmdoc/parse.go:840-859) builds the alt from children of type `text` and `image` alone, so a child this change newly makes an `html` node contributes nothing; `mdast-util-to-string`, which the comment above it names as the rule it follows, writes a literal node's own value. Red test: `TestParseKeepsRawHTMLInAnImageAltText` in packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/pmdoc/parse_test.go, committed on this branch; `go test ./internal/dispatch/pmdoc/ -run '^TestParseKeepsRawHTMLInAnImageAltText$' -count=1` fails at this head, the first three rows being this regression (`alt of "![p <!a> q](i.png)
" = "p  q", want "p <!a> q"`).

failures.criterion: The same reading rule for every other kind of raw HTML in an image label, which main drops too: the engine keeps `<b>`, `<!A>`, `<!-- c -->`, `<?x?>` and `<![CDATA[x]]>` in an image's alt and Go keeps none of them, so a comment and a document holding `![r <b> s](i.png)` read differently at main and at this head.
failures.evidence: Measured in this pod on 2026-10-29: the two revisions' dumps give `![r <b> s](i.png)` the rendering `![r  s](i.png)` at both, and the same for `<!A>`, `<!-- c -->`, `<?x?>` and `<![CDATA[x]]>`; the engine (gen/differential.ts) reads each alt as written (`r <b> s` and so on). Not a regression - main has it - but the same line of `parseImage` and the same divergence class this pull request exists to close, so the one-arm fix for the entry above closes it, and the last five rows of the red test `TestParseKeepsRawHTMLInAnImageAltText` pin it. Its consequence for A3: keeping raw HTML in the alt changes the reading of a stored version that holds one, so the census must be re-read at the fixed head with a candidate filter for an image label holding raw HTML. I measured that filter over all 33,614 distinct stored markdowns of the crawl: 5 match (`![<h`, `![<n`), and every one of the 8 occurrences sits inside a code span in this tree's own plan or issue text, so the fix changes no stored version in production either. If the architect rules this half out of scope, the last five rows of the red test are the rows to drop; the first three are the regression and stay.
